paper_title: SRPO Enhancing Multimodal LLM Reasoning via Reflection-Aware   Reinforcement Learning
caption: : RL training data statistic

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of samples across different categories of reinforcement learning (RL) training data, as presented in the context of the SRPO method for enhancing multimodal LLM reasoning. The horizontal axis displays five distinct categories: "Other Math," "Geometric Math," "Charts Diagrams," "Natural Science," and "General Reasoning," arranged in descending order of sample count from left to right. The vertical axis, labeled "Number of Samples," represents the quantity of data entries and is scaled linearly from 0 to 14,000, with major tick marks at intervals of 2,000. Each bar corresponds to a category and is labeled with its exact sample count above the bar. The tallest bar, representing "Other Math," reaches a value of 14,333. The subsequent bars show decreasing values: "Geometric Math" at 10,227, "Charts Diagrams" at 5,953, "Natural Science" at 3,343, and "General Reasoning" at 3,534. The bars are uniformly colored in a light orange shade and are positioned side-by-side, clearly separating the categories.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart, titled "RL training data statistic," illustrates the number of samples across five different categories of training data used in the SRPO method for enhancing multimodal LLM reasoning. The vertical axis, labeled "Number of Samples," ranges from 0 to 14,000 with major gridlines at intervals of 2,000. The horizontal axis lists the categories: "Other Math," "Geometric Math," "Charts Diagrams," "Natural Science," and "General Reasoning." Each category is represented by a single orange bar, with the exact count of samples displayed as a label on top of each bar. The "Other Math" category has the highest number of samples at 14,333. "Geometric Math" follows with 10,227 samples. "Charts Diagrams" has 5,953 samples, "Natural Science" has 3,343, and "General Reasoning" has 3,534. The bars are arranged in descending order of sample count from left to right.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm zeigt die Anzahl der Proben für verschiedene Kategorien von RL-Trainingsdaten, wobei die vertikale Achse die „Number of Samples“ (Anzahl der Proben) in einem linearen Skalierungsverlauf von 0 bis 14.000 in Schritten von 2.000 darstellt. Die horizontale Achse listet fünf Kategorien auf: „Other Math“, „Geometric Math“, „Charts Diagrams“, „Natural Science“ und „General Reasoning“. Jede Kategorie ist durch einen orangefarbenen Balken repräsentiert, dessen Höhe den entsprechenden Probenwert visualisiert. Der höchste Balken entspricht der Kategorie „Other Math“ mit 14.333 Proben, gefolgt von „Geometric Math“ mit 10.227 Proben, „Charts Diagrams“ mit 5.953 Proben, „Natural Science“ mit 3.343 Proben und „General Reasoning“ mit 3.534 Proben. Die Balken sind in absteigender Reihenfolge nach der Anzahl der Proben angeordnet, wobei keine visuellen Hervorhebungen oder zusätzlichen grafischen Elemente wie Schattierungen oder Beschriftungen außer den numerischen Werten über den Balken vorhanden sind.
